name: project-index
question: Does this project's CLAUDE.md hold the shape the instruction-surface standard asks for, and how big is it getting?

assertion.asserts: the project index carries what a fresh session's first hour needs and nothing that belongs in git, a dev note or a linked authority (ISF-2, ISF-3), and its size is visible as a trend before it becomes a problem (ISF-7)
assertion.measures: four deterministic SHAPES over the index text, each a `fail`: a block whose opening word is a finished-work token; a body inlined under a `## Pending Follow-Ups` stub (a nested bullet, a blank-separated paragraph, a sub-heading or a fenced block inside the section); a stub over `FOLLOWUP_STUB_BYTES`; and a paragraph whose 10-word shingles overlap the RENDERED global instruction file at `<home>/CLAUDE.md` by at least 25%. Plus three `warn` measures: bytes over `PROJECT_INDEX_ALARM_BYTES` (or the project's `.claude/config.json` `limits.project_index_alarm_bytes`), growth over `PROJECT_INDEX_GROWTH_BYTES` against the previous committed size, and a backticked token that looks like a path and resolves to nothing in the tree
known_gaps: THE FINISHED-WORK TOKENS ARE A PROXY FOR NARRATION, AND A PARAPHRASE PASSES. The fail is a fixed list of past-tense openers matched at the first word of a block. `Completed the migration to v2` fails; `The migration to v2 is complete` says the same thing and passes, and so does any narration that opens with a noun. The shape catches the form the diet reports actually found -- a changelog entry pasted into an index -- and claims nothing about narration in general. Widening the list is how it stops being deterministic; the judgment half of ISF-2 reaches the author by delivered segment instead.

SHAPE 4 COMPARES AGAINST THE RENDERED GLOBAL FILE, WHICH MAY BE ABSENT OR STALE. `<home>/CLAUDE.md` is written by `sync.py`; on a machine that has never synced it does not exist, and the shape is then not measured at all -- reported as a `warn` naming the absence, never skipped silently. When it is present it is the DEPLOYED text, so a global rule edited in the template and not yet synced is compared against the old wording.

SHAPE 4 CANNOT TELL A RESTATEMENT FROM A DELIBERATE QUOTATION. A project that quotes a global rule on purpose -- to say it is tightened here, or to name the authority verbatim -- trips the same overlap as one that pasted it in. The direction is deliberate: the index is an index, and a rule that needs the global file's own words needs a pointer to the global file. A project that means it moves the quotation into the linked authority or accepts the fail's fix.

SIZE AND GROWTH ARE `warn` AND NOTHING FAILS ON EITHER (DEC-472). An index growing without bound is visible in every session-start briefing and stopped by no gate. That is the trade: the byte FAIL this replaces produced cut-to-fit in three of five files in one afternoon, one of them reporting 12 KB of its own content unreachable under the wall.

GROWTH IS MEASURED AGAINST ONE PRIOR SIZE, NOT A TREND. When the working tree differs from HEAD the delta is this uncommitted change's; otherwise it is the last commit's (HEAD vs HEAD~1). A sawtooth of six commits each adding 1.9 KB never warns, and neither does a rewrite that adds 8 KB while deleting 8 KB. It is an alarm on the single jump the diet reports measured, not a regression on the curve.

THE BACKTICKED-PATH WARN RESOLVES BY EXISTENCE ONLY, AND SKIPS ANYTHING AMBIGUOUS. A token holding a glob, a placeholder (`<home>`), a `~` or an absolute path is not graded at all, so a whole class of stale pointer is invisible. A token that resolves is not checked for being the RIGHT file.

SHAPES ARE GRADED OVER THE FILE'S TEXT, NOT A MARKDOWN PARSE. Blocks are split on blank lines and fenced code is tracked well enough to keep a fence's contents out of the block scan; a document that nests fences inside lists inside fences can confuse the split. A confused split can only mis-attribute a line to a neighbouring block, never invent a token that is not in the file.
